title: Undercity
body: Beneath the broken capital of Lordaeron lies the Undercity, seat of the Forsaken. The old kingdom kept its royal crypts, catacombs, dungeons and sewers here, under the palace of its kings, and the poorest of its people lived in the gloom below. The Scourge began carving these depths into a stronghold, but Arthas left the work unfinished when he was called north. When Sylvanas Windrunner broke free and turned on the dreadlords who ruled the ruins, her Forsaken claimed the warren and finished it as their own. Lifts descend from the ruined palace to the Trade Quarter at its heart, ringed by the Magic Quarter, the Rogues' Quarter, the War Quarter and the Apothecarium, with foul canals running between them and the Royal Quarter beyond. The city has only lately been won back. After the treachery at the Wrathgate, Varimathras and Grand Apothecary Putress seized it in a bloody coup, and Thrall and Sylvanas retook it by force. Now Kor'kron orcs walk its halls, sent to guard the Forsaken and to watch them.

title: The Elevators
body: Three great lifts join the ruined palace of Lordaeron to the Trade Quarter far below, the main road between the open ruins and the city of the dead. Travelers ride them down long, dark shafts, and their doors close so quickly that the careless learn to step lively. The lifts were a prize in the Battle for the Undercity. The rebels wrecked the way down and trapped the shaft, and Sylvanas warned that a fall would mean certain death. Thrall answered by calling on the spirits of air, and cyclones lowered the Horde's champions safely into the inner sanctum below.

title: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner
body: Once Ranger-General of Silvermoon, Sylvanas Windrunner fell defending Quel'Thalas from Arthas and was raised as a banshee in his service. When the Lich King's grip faltered she broke free, turned on the dreadlords who held Lordaeron and named her freed undead the Forsaken. She rules them from the Royal Quarter, curt with visitors, for the city does not run itself. She championed the blood elves' entry into the Horde, and sends her chosen to Nathanos Blightcaller, one of her first champions. Betrayed by Varimathras and Putress after the Wrathgate, she barely escaped with her life, then returned beside Thrall to take back her throne.

title: Varimathras
body: Varimathras was one of three dreadlord brothers who ruled Lordaeron's undead for the Burning Legion after Arthas went north. When Sylvanas broke his forces he begged for his life and offered his service, and for years he stood at her side in the Royal Quarter as her lieutenant, with the Deathstalkers first serving as his elite guard. His loyalty was a mask. After the Wrathgate he and Putress seized the Undercity and loosed demons and blight on its defenders. Cornered in the throne room by Thrall and Sylvanas, he raged over years of wasted planning and begged pardon of an unseen Master before the Dark Lady struck him down.

title: Grand Apothecary Putress
body: Grand Apothecary Putress rose to lead the Royal Apothecary Society after winning Sylvanas's favor with a vow to take the plague that made the Forsaken and make it their own weapon. From the Apothecarium his chemists refined the New Plague, a blight lethal to living and undead alike, and the Horde even credited him with finding a cure for a recent outbreak of the Scourge's own plague. At the Wrathgate he turned his blight on Alliance, Horde and Scourge together, striking down Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and many soldiers. With Varimathras he then seized the Undercity. When King Varian's forces broke into his laboratory, Putress tried to swallow ever more power, raving that he saw everything, and died there.

title: Master Apothecary Faranell
body: Master Apothecary Faranell leads the Royal Apothecary Society from the Apothecarium, overseeing its most ambitious and most ghoulish work: guano from the bats of Razorfen Kraul, hearts cut from Scarlet zealots, venoms and composites sent home by his apothecaries in the field. He speaks of it all with unsettling delight. Since Putress's betrayal the Society labors under the eye of the Warchief's Kor'kron, and Faranell has turned diplomat, assuring his overseer that the apothecaries wish only to make amends for a tragic misguidance and to continue their research in peace. Putress, he insists, was an unfortunate anomaly.

title: Bragor Bloodfist
body: Bragor Bloodfist is a Kor'kron captain sent by Thrall to stand at the Dark Lady's side after the city was retaken. With most of the Forsaken army committed to Vengeance Landing in Northrend, the Warchief's guard now reinforces the Undercity, and Bragor has taken up many duties once held by Varimathras: sending agents against the Scarlet Crusade, receiving word from the Hillsbrad front, and hunting a Scourge emissary named Malcin near Razorfen Downs. A living orc among the dead, he keeps dangerous books from the Forsaken as carefully as from the Shadow Council. He judges newcomers by their deeds, and already counts the human king among the threats the Horde must one day end.

title: Overseer Kraggosh
body: Overseer Kraggosh is the Kor'kron orc posted inside the Apothecarium itself, and he makes no secret of how little he likes it. Since Putress loosed his blight at the Wrathgate, the Warchief has trusted the Royal Apothecary Society about as far as he could throw it, and Kraggosh is the result: no abomination guards, no secrecy, no plotting in the dark. The apothecaries can do nothing without him, and he has warned Master Apothecary Faranell that if the Society so much as spits without leave, the place will be shut down by force. His fellow overseers stand watch across the city and treat the Forsaken with open contempt.

title: Sharlindra
body: Sharlindra is a banshee of the Dark Lady's court and long in her service. She was present when Varimathras offered Sylvanas a place in his new order, and privately wondered whether accepting might have been the wiser course. She fought beside the Forsaken when they stormed the stronghold of the dreadlord Detheroc. Today she keeps to the Royal Quarter and directs agents abroad through lieutenants such as Melisara at Tarren Mill. When the ogre Mug'Thol stole the Crown of Will meant for Sylvanas, and the Dark Lady wanted an example made, it was Sharlindra who set the task in motion.

title: Parqual Fintallas
body: Before the plague took him, Parqual Fintallas was a great historian of Lordaeron's human kingdom. Death has not cured him of scholarship. He lingers in the Undercity still seeking enlightenment, though of a different kind, and holds that knowledge of the world will outlast mere strength. To those who would prove their minds he sets a final test of lore, sending them first to the Scarlet Monastery for a book its zealots once used to train paladins against his kind. His question, fittingly, concerns the very creature that became the Lich King and spread the plague across Lordaeron.

title: Apothecary Zinge
body: Apothecary Zinge of the Royal Apothecary Society has a sharp eye for opportunity, especially other people's. By her account Apothecary Keever, at work in the next room, is touched in the head, yet his research might bear fruit if pursued by a clever researcher, and Zinge means to be that researcher. She sends her errand runners to Alessandro Luca of Blue Moon Odds and Ends, who pines for her company, and on to the Tanaris desert to test the flesh of basilisks, scorpids and hyenas. She rewards those who stay useful, and corresponds with colleagues as far afield as the Crossroads and Kargath.

title: The Battle for the Undercity
body: The blight that fell on the Wrathgate was not the end of the treachery. Grand Apothecary Putress and the dreadlord Varimathras had turned much of the Forsaken against their queen, and they seized the Undercity. Sylvanas barely escaped to Orgrimmar, those who would not side with the rebels were executed or banished, and Orgrimmar, now under martial law, took in the Forsaken refugees. Thrall vowed justice. Through portals from Grommash Hold the Horde gathered at the ruins with Vol'jin, then fought down past a wrecked lift and a trapped shaft into the Royal Quarter, where Varimathras fell. Meanwhile King Varian Wrynn, Jaina Proudmoore, Broll Bearmantle and Valeera Sanguinar led the Alliance through the sewers, hunting Putress to his death in the Apothecarium. Then Varian marched on the throne room and turned his blades on Thrall. Only Jaina's magic, freezing the combatants and carrying the Alliance away, prevented a slaughter. The old fellowship of the Wrathgate did not survive the day.

title: The Lady's Necklace
body: In the Ghostlands, a necklace was recovered from the Scourge near Windrunner Spire, bright against the gloom and inscribed as the property of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. High Executor Mavren at Tranquillien saw that it was a gift to her from her sister Alleria, and sent it on to the Royal Quarter. Sylvanas seized it, startled into memory, then mastered herself and scorned the gift. Alleria, she declared, was a long dead memory, and the trinket meant nothing to the queen of the Forsaken. She let it fall to the floor and dismissed the bearer. Yet a moment later she knelt and took it up again. Whispering 'Belore', she wove a glamour that called forth the spirits of the Highborne, and the throne room filled with their ancient song of the sin'dorei.

title: The Crown of Will
body: Lady Sylvanas desired the Crown of Will, a relic to be had in Alterac, and sent the ogre Mug'Thol and his Crushridge warband to fetch it, bound to her service by possession. Mug'Thol found the crown and, being an ogre, could not resist putting it on. Its power let him throw off the Dark Lady's will, and his Crushridge overran the ruins of Alterac. The Dark Lady wanted an example made, and Sharlindra of the Royal Quarter passed the task to her lieutenant Melisara at Tarren Mill. Melisara had the Crushridge thinned, then claimed the heads of Mug'Thol's lieutenants Targ, Muckrake and Glommus, and at last Mug'Thol's own, meaning to mount all four on pikes above Alterac. The crown itself returned to Sharlindra, to be laid before the queen it was always meant for.
sources: quests 495, 518, 519, 520 and 521 (descriptions and reward text)
notes: Quest 495: the Dark Lady, not Sharlindra, wants the example made; fixed. Most of the chain runs in Alterac and Hillsbrad; another zone's codex may also cover it.

title: The Deathstalkers
body: Promising rogues of the Horde may be summoned to the Rogues' Quarter by Mennet Carkad, who tests candidates for the Deathstalkers, the Dark Lady's elite agents. The test is a quiet one. Their leaders suspect Andron Gant, a merchant whose shop stands by the Apothecarium, of selling secrets to some other power. First the candidate must obtain, by whatever means suits, the letter of introduction carried by Astor Hadren, a courier between Silverpine and the Undercity. Posing as the expected messenger, the recruit calls on Andron, who suspects nothing and hands over his ledger with his regards. The ledger names his true buyers: the Syndicate, proof of how far the lords of Alterac have fallen since their betrayal. Carkad welcomes the recruit into the Deathstalkers and sends the new agent to carry the findings to Aleric Hawkins, their master in the Royal Quarter.
sources: quests 1885, 14420, 14419, 14421 and 14418 (descriptions, log text and reward text)

title: Seeping Corruption
body: In the Apothecarium, Chemist Cuely keeps a patient who did not come to be studied. Thersa Windsong, a tauren, was wounded by naga in the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara and afterward drank from a tide pool on the beach. She has been sick ever since, and no priest or shaman could help her. Cuely, more accommodating than she finds comfortable, has a helper fill labeled vials at the pools so he can learn what she drank. From the samples he brews an elixir and has it carried to her. With nowhere else to turn, Thersa drinks and prays that the Earthmother will watch over her spirit. The elixir takes hold faster than even Cuely dreamed, and she does not survive it. Pleased, the chemist turns at once to the remaining samples, certain they will soon be of use to Lady Sylvanas.
sources: quests 3568, 3569 and 3570 (descriptions and reward text)

title: The Jeremiah Blues
body: Among the records the Forsaken keep, few are stranger than the city census. Royal Overseer Bauhaus tends it by arcane means and disciplined mind, tracking the populace since the city was freed from the Scourge. When a dusty parcel turned up in the Plaguelands, addressed more than four years earlier to one Jeremiah Felstone of Lordaeron, the census held the answer. Like some Forsaken, Felstone had shed his old name with his old life, and now sold cockroaches as Jeremiah Payson beneath a walkway near the bank. He took the visit badly, since the sender was his sister Janice, dead these four years, until he saw the parcel truly came from her. Inside lay the deed to the Felstone farm, which he declined to reclaim, and half of a good luck charm, which he asked be returned to her restless spirit.
